# Wilcoxon rank-sum test

Independent 2 samples

Also known as the Mann-Whitney U test

## Wilcoxon rank-sum test

Developed by [Frank Wilcoxon](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frank_Wilcoxon) the rank-sum test is an [nonparametric](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nonparametric_statistics) alternative to the independent samples t-test.

By ranking all values and then summing the ranks per group, one would expect under the null hypothesis, that the sum of ranks is approximately equal.

After standardizing the test statistic (summed ranks for one group), we can use the standard normal distribution as the sampling distribution.


```{r wrs-wilcoxon-rank-sum-test, echo=FALSE}
set.seed(123)
n      <- 20
factor <- rep(c("Ecstasy","Alcohol"),each=n/2)
dummy  <- ifelse(factor == "Ecstacy", 0, 1)
b.0    <- 23
b.1    <- 5
error  <- rnorm(n, 0, 1.7)
depres <- b.0 + b.1*dummy + error
depres <- round(depres)

data <- data.frame(factor, depres)
data <- read.csv(datasetsPath("drug_long.csv"))[, -3]
data$Drug <- ifelse(data$Drug == 1, "Ecstasy", "Alcohol")
## add the ranks
data$rankedBDI <- rank(data$Sunday.BDI)
```


## Example
`r dsjLinks("drug_long")`

```{r wrs-example, echo=FALSE}
ssrTable(data, height = 300,
          options = list(dom = 'Bfrtip',
                         buttons = c('csv')))
```

## Q-Q plot of the residuals {.smaller}

Sunday BDI, independent $t$-test in JASP: Assumption Checks → Q-Q plot residuals → Confidence interval^[The book (Figure 15.4) checks the raw scores per group, with separate Q-Q plots from the Descriptives module. Its Q-Q plots (also Figures 15.10 and 15.13) have no confidence band, which JASP added later.]

More on this in the [extra text on skewed data](https://johnnydoorn.github.io/teaching-statistics/extra-texts/violating-assumptions-anova.html#t-test-with-skewed-data) (Student, Welch or Mann-Whitney?)

```{r wrs-qq-plot, echo=FALSE, fig.width=6, fig.height=4.5, out.width='390px', fig.align='center'}
groupMeans <- tapply(data$Sunday.BDI, data$Drug, mean)
qqJasp(as.vector(scale(data$Sunday.BDI - groupMeans[data$Drug])))
```


## Test statistic W is the sum of ranks per group {.subsection .smaller}

```{r wrs-rank-sums, echo=TRUE}
rankSums <- aggregate(rankedBDI ~ Drug, data, sum)
rankSums
```

We can take the sum of ranks for the first group as W:  

```{r wrs-w-statistic, echo=TRUE}
W <- rankSums[1, 2]
W
```

## Subtracting the minimum score {.smaller}

JASP reports the value of U, which is W with its minimum value subtracted:

```{r wrs-subtracting-the-minimum-score, echo=TRUE}
W.min <- sum(1:10); W.min

U <- W - W.min
U
```

```{r wrs-u-ecstasy, echo=FALSE}
U.ecstasy <- rankSums[rankSums$Drug == "Ecstasy", 2] - W.min
```

- JASP (and the book) take the ecstasy group: `r rankSums[rankSums$Drug == "Ecstasy", 2]` - `r W.min` = `r U.ecstasy`
- The two add up to $n_1 n_2$ = `r U + U.ecstasy`

## Normal approximation for W

To calculate the Z-score we need to standardize the W. To do so we need the mean W and the standard error of W.

For this we need the sample sizes for each group.

```{r wrs-normal-approximation-for-w, echo=TRUE}
n <- aggregate(rankedBDI ~ factor, data, length)

n.1 <- n$rankedBDI[1]
n.2 <- n$rankedBDI[2]

cbind(n.1, n.2)
```

## Mean W under $H_0$ {.smaller}

$$\bar{W}_s=\frac{n_1(n_1+n_2+1)}{2}$$
  
```{r wrs-mean-w-under, echo=TRUE}
W.mean <- (n.1 * (n.1 + n.2 + 1)) / 2
W.mean # this is the middle point between the min and max value of W

W.max <- sum(11:20); W.max
W.min <- sum(1:10); W.min
```

## SE W

$${SE}_{\bar{W}_s}=\sqrt{ \frac{n_1 n_2 (n_1+n_2+1)}{12} }$$
  
```{r wrs-se-w, echo=TRUE}
W.se <- sqrt((n.1 * n.2 * (n.1 + n.2 + 1)) / 12)
W.se
```

## Calculate Z {.subsection .smaller}

$$z = \frac{W - \bar{W}}{{SE}_W}$$
  
Which looks a lot like

$$\frac{X - \bar{X}}{{SE}_X} \text{or} \frac{b - \mu_{b}}{{SE}_b} $$
  
```{r wrs-calculate-z, echo=TRUE}
z <- (W - W.mean) / W.se
z
```

## Test for significance 2 sided

```{r wrs-test-for-significance-2-sided, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, fig.align='center'}
visualize_normal_base(z, side = "two-sided")
```

```{r wrs-jasp-p, echo=FALSE}
jaspMW <- suppressWarnings(wilcox.test(Sunday.BDI ~ factor(Drug, levels = c("Ecstasy", "Alcohol")), data = data))
```

JASP: *U* = `r jaspMW$statistic`, *p* = `r sub("^0", "", sprintf("%.3f", jaspMW$p.value))`, a bit higher because of a continuity correction (Jane Superbrain 15.2)


## Test for significance 1 sided

```{r wrs-test-for-significance-1-sided, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, fig.align='center'}
visualize_normal_base(z, side = "negative")
```



## Effect size rank-biserial correlation

$$r_{bs} = 1 - \frac{2*W}{n_1*n_2}$$
  
```{r wrs-effect-size-rank-biserial-correlation, echo=TRUE}
W <- W - W.min # use modern W
biserialCor <- 1 - (2*(W)) / (n.1*n.2);
biserialCor
```


## Robustness under monotonic transformations

```{r wrs-monotonic-transformation-data, echo = FALSE, message=FALSE }
set.seed(123)
n <- 20
y <- runif(n, 0, 0.5)
gr <- factor(rep(letters[1:2], each = n /2))
y[gr == "a"] <- y[gr == "a"] + 0.18
y <- 1-y



y1 <- y^2
y1Stats <- c(t.test(y1 ~ gr)$statistic, wilcox.test(y1 ~ gr)$statistic)


y2 <- qnorm(y)
y2Stats <- c(t.test(y2 ~ gr)$statistic, wilcox.test(y2 ~ gr)$statistic)



y3 <- log(y, base = 20)
y3Stats <- c(t.test(y3 ~ gr)$statistic, wilcox.test(y3 ~ gr)$statistic)



y4 <- qt(y, 1)
y4Stats <- c(t.test(y4 ~ gr)$statistic, wilcox.test(y4 ~ gr)$statistic)


yList <- list(y1, y2, y3, y4)
```

```{r wrs-monotonic-transformation-plots, echo= FALSE}
par(mfrow = c(2, 2), cex = 1, bty = "n")
plotCex<- 1
boxplot(y2 ~ gr, xlab = "Condition", ylab = "DV", col = c("darkgreen", "darkorange"),
        main= "Normal", cex = plotCex)
mtext(side = 3, paste0("t = ", (round(y2Stats[1], 2)), 
                       "\nW = ", (round(y2Stats[2], 2))), adj = 1)
boxplot(y1 ~ gr, xlab = "Condition", ylab = "DV", col = c("darkgreen", "darkorange"),
        main= "y^2", cex =plotCex )
mtext(side = 3, paste0("t = ", (round(y1Stats[1], 2)), 
                       "\nW = ", (round(y1Stats[2], 2))), adj = 1)
boxplot(y3 ~ gr, xlab = "Condition", ylab = "DV", col = c("darkgreen", "darkorange"),
        main= "log(y)", cex = plotCex)
mtext(side = 3, paste0("t = ", (round(y3Stats[1], 2)), 
                       "\nW = ", (round(y3Stats[2], 2))), adj = 1)
boxplot(y4 ~ gr, xlab = "Condition", ylab = "DV", col = c("darkgreen", "darkorange"),
        main= "Cauchy", cex = plotCex, ylim = c(0, 16))
mtext(side = 3, paste0("t = ", (round(y4Stats[1], 2)), 
                       "\nW = ", (round(y4Stats[2], 2))), adj = 1)


```
